newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Grains futures rise in busy Budapest market.
newsitem.headline: Grains futures rise in busy Budapest market.

text.p: A mostly limit-up rise in milling wheat futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) on Thursday was triggered by one market player, a trader said.
"One market participant met all offers for August at the closing, and the rise cascaded through all subsequent maturities," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle.
He added that most traders followed the trend due to lack of other information to trade on.
"Most traders thought the buyer must have had a good reason to do so," Herczeg said.

August milling wheat went up 380 forints per tonne to end at 21,980 forints while September, October and December put on the daily allowed 400 forints to close at 22,400, 22,800 and 23,570 forints, respectively.

Feed barley prices rose by 250 forints for July and 100 for August to finish at 18,690 and 18,850 but Herczeg said the increase was only in response to the wheat price rise as barley usually follows the latter.
Maize prices rose by between 100 and 300 forints for all but October with the nearest and most distant maturity accounting for the bulk of the turnover.
May prices had the sharpest rise to 18,400 forints, up 300, as traders began to close their positions, Herczeg said.
Total grains turnover was 613.7 million forints or 1,489 contracts, with milling wheat accounting for 812 and maize for 571 contracts.
This was a relatively high turnover for this season, Herczeg said.
"This period is tradionally one of the more quiet parts of the year and trade will really pick up only in May," he said.
